requirement:
When `habeas author` assesses a subject with existing evidence, that evidence
MUST only determine whether the subject needs assessment. Its inputs,
determination, and rationale MUST NOT contribute to the mandatory input set
defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` or otherwise be
supplied to the model. A new assessment's evidence MUST record only the inputs
supplied to it, so sources that an earlier assessment read but that no longer
exist or are no longer relevant cannot block or shape reassessment.
rationale:
I found no gap. All four obligations are met by code reachable from the `{impl}` item, and each has a `{test}`-marked test.

**Implementation.** `author_all_with_options` (src/authoring/batch.rs:45) carries the `{impl}`. It calls `run_batch`, which reaches `select_subjects`, `prepare_assessment` and `AssessmentSources::prepare`.

**Obligations and code**
- **Existing evidence MUST only determine whether the subject needs assessment.**
  - `select_subjects` (batch.rs:472) is the only place `run_batch` consults existing evidence. It loads the record with `LoadedDetailEvidence::load`, checks `current(&evidence)`, and either counts the subject as unchanged or queues it.
  - `AssessmentSources::prepare` (inputs.rs:73) never reads the evidence file. A comment there says existing evidence only decides whether to reassess.
- **Earlier inputs, determination and rationale MUST NOT contribute to the mandatory input set or be supplied to the model.**
  - `prepare` builds `mandatory` only from the subject's declaration, its `{cite}` targets, its `{impl}`, `{test}` and `{fixme}` edges, anchors, term dependencies and built-ins.
  - `generated_evidence_selector` filters out `evidence/` selectors, and generated-evidence references are omitted by default.
  - `model_mandatory_inputs` derives only from `self.mandatory`, so nothing from the old record reaches the model.
- **A new assessment's evidence MUST record only the inputs supplied to it.**
  - `AssessmentSources.recorded` starts empty, and `record_inputs` (called from `converse`) adds only the inputs delivered to the model.
  - `record()` (mod.rs:1126) writes `sources.recorded_inputs()` as the record's `inputs`.
- **Stale sources that no longer exist cannot block or shape reassessment.** Because `prepare` ignores old inputs, missing files, items and requirements named in them cause no error.

**Tests, each carrying a `{test}` reference to the subject**
- `unresolvable_earlier_inputs_do_not_block_reassessment` (inputs.rs:963) writes old evidence naming a missing file, a removed Rust item and a removed requirement. It asserts that `prepare` still succeeds and the mandatory set is exactly the subject's declaration.
- `earlier_evidence_inputs_and_judgments_are_not_carried_forward` (inputs.rs:994) asserts that the supplied inputs contain no `notes.txt`, no `evidence/` path and no old rationale, and that the old record file is unchanged.
- `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors` (inputs.rs:870) asserts the same exclusions alongside a full bundle. It also asserts `sources.recorded_inputs().is_empty()` after `prepare`, so old evidence inputs are not recorded.

**Weaker coverage.** The batch-selection tests (`selection_counts_…`, `selection_includes_site_reviews…`) and the recording tests (mod.rs:1746, tools.rs) exercise related behavior but carry no `{test}` reference to this requirement. The marked tests still cover each obligation, so I do not count this as a gap.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When `habeas author` assesses a subject with existing evidence, that evidence
MUST only determine whether the subject needs assessment. Its inputs,
determination, and rationale MUST NOT contribute to the mandatory input set
defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` or otherwise be
supplied to the model. A new assessment's evidence MUST record only the inputs
supplied to it, so sources that an earlier assessment read but that no longer
exist or are no longer relevant cannot block or shape reassessment.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
